'''Bettye Washington Greene''' (March 20, 1935 – June 16, 1995) was an American industrial research [[chemist]]. She was one of the first few African American women to earn her Ph.D. in chemistry and she was the first [[African American]] female Ph.D. chemist to work in a professional position at the [[Dow Chemical Company]]. At Dow, she researched [[latex]] and [[polymer]]s.<ref name=Othmeralia /> Greene is considered an early African American pioneer in science.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-05-04|title=The Complete List of Genius Black Inventors, Scientists and Engineers That Changed the World|url=https://interestingengineering.com/black-inventors-the-complete-list-of-genius-black-american-african-american-inventors-scientists-and-engineers-with-their-revolutionary-inventions-that-changed-the-world-and-impacted-the-history-part-one|access-date=2020-07-12|website=interestingengineering.com|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life ==

Bettye Washington was born to George Washington and Kian Criss in Palestine, Texas, where she attended Our Lady of Mercy Elementary School and James E. Guinn Junior High School.<ref name=":0" /> She attended [[School segregation in the United States|segregated public schools]] and graduated from [[I.M. Terrell High School]] around 1952.

== Education ==
She entered [[Tuskegee University|Tuskegee Institute]] in Alabama, graduating with a B.S. in chemistry in 1955. She attended [[Wayne State University]] in [[Detroit|Detroit, Michigan]], where she earned her Ph.D. in [[physical chemistry]] working with [[Wilfried Heller]] (1965). Her doctoral research provided new knowledge in evaluating light scattering methods to determine the size of particles.<ref>{{ cite book|last=Collins |first=Sibrina N. |chapter=Dr. Bettye Washington Greene: From Tuskegee to the Dow Chemical Company | title=African American chemists: academia, industry, and social entrepreneurship |date=2021 |series=ACS Symposium Series |volume=1381 |pages=9–18 |editor-last=Collins |editor-first=Sibrina N. |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/bk-2021-1381.ch002 |access-date=2024-12-04 |place=Washington, DC |publisher=American Chemical Society |language=en |doi=10.1021/bk-2021-1381.ch002 |isbn=978-0-8412-9838-5|url-access=subscription }}</ref> She also taught undergraduate chemistry at this time. Her doctoral dissertation, "[https://www.proquest.com/docview/302322645?pq-origsite=gscholar&fromopenview=true&sourcetype=Dissertations%20&%20Theses Determination of particle size distributions in emulsions by light scattering]" was published in 1965.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Brundidge |first1=Clinique |last2=Cooper |first2=Valentino R. |date=2022 |title=Bettye Washington Greene: An Industrial Chemist and Inventor Who Lit a Path for Innovation |url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11837-021-05128-5.pdf |journal=JOM |volume=74 |issue=2 |pages=334–336|doi=10.1007/s11837-021-05128-5 }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
She married Veteran Air Force Captain William Miller Greene in July 1955. She had three children: [[Willetta Greene Johnson]], Victor M. Greene, and Lisa Kianne Greene. She was elected to [[Sigma Xi]], the Scientific Research Society. She had no siblings.

==Career==
=== Dow Chemical ===

In 1965, Greene joined the Dow Chemical Company's E. C. Britton Research Laboratory in [[Midland, Michigan]]. She was the first African-American woman to join the company in a professional position.<ref name=Othmeralia /> Greene served as a Consultant on Polymers issues in the Saran Research Laboratory and the Styrene Butadiene (SB) Latex group often utilized her expertise and knowledge.<ref name="Science History Institute Digital Collections">{{Cite web|title=Dr. Bettye Washington Greene (1935-1995)|url=https://digital.sciencehistory.org/works/t722h939f|access-date=2020-06-10|website=Science History Institute Digital Collections|language=en}}</ref> At Dow, she researched [[colloid]] and [[latex]] chemistry, including interactions between latex and paper.<ref name="Warren">{{cite book |last=Warren |first=Wini |url=https://archive.org/details/blackwomenscient00warr |title=Black women scientists in the United States |date=1999 |publisher=Indiana University Press |isbn=0253336031 |location=Bloomington, Ind. [u.a.] |pages=[https://archive.org/details/blackwomenscient00warr/page/109 109]–110 |url-access=registration}}</ref>

In 1970, Greene was promoted to senior research chemist at Dow Chemical. In 1973, she joined Dow Chemical's Designed Polymers Research Division, again working with latex, to find [[polymers]] that could improve latex.<ref name="Warren" /> She was subsequently promoted to the position of senior research specialist in 1975.<ref name="Science History Institute Digital Collections" /> She continued to work for Dow Chemical until her retirement in 1990.<ref name=Othmeralia /><ref name=Warren /><ref name="Blacksciencefictionsociety-2020">{{Cite web|date=2020-02-17|title=Dr. Bettye Washington Greene...|url=https://blacksciencefictionsociety.com/profiles/blogs/dr-bettye-washington-greene|access-date=2020-06-10|website=Blacksciencefictionsociety}}</ref> She published several papers studying different properties that lend to the redispersement of latex.<ref name="9 black chemists you should know about">{{Cite web|title=9 black chemists you should know about|url=https://cen.acs.org/people/profiles/Six-black-chemists-should-know/97/web/2019/02|access-date=2020-06-10|website=9 black chemists you should know about|language=en}}</ref> She also published work studying methodologies for determining the surface tension of liquids or solutions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Heller|first1=Wilfried|last2=Cheng|first2=Mien-Hsiung|last3=Greene|first3=Bettye W|date=1966-08-01|title=Surface tension measurements by means of the "microcone tensiometer"|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0021-9797%2866%2990082-8|journal=Journal of Colloid and Interface Science|language=en|volume=22|issue=2|pages=179–194|doi=10.1016/0021-9797(66)90082-8|pmid=5983141 |bibcode=1966JCIS...22..179H |issn=0021-9797|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She left Dow Chemical in 1990.

Greene filed for several patents during her career at Dow Chemical. In 1985, she was issued a patent entitled "Stable latexes containing phosphorus surface groups" describing a method of preparing a paper coating composition comprising the addition of from about 2 to about 30 percent of a modified latex containing phosphorus surface groups.<ref>{{Cite web|title=US Patent for Stable latexes containing phosphorus surface groups Patent (Patent # 4,506,057 issued March 19, 1985) - Justia Patents Search|url=https://patents.justia.com/patent/4506057|access-date=2020-08-16|website=patents.justia.com}}</ref> In 1986, she was issued a follow-up patent entitled "Composite sheet prepared with stable latexes containing phosphorus surface groups" also employing emulsion polymerization techniques for preparing modified latex.<ref>{{Cite web|title=US Patent for Composite sheet prepared with stable latexes containing phosphorus surface groups Patent (Patent # 4,609,434 issued September 2, 1986) - Justia Patents Search|url=https://patents.justia.com/patent/4609434|access-date=2020-08-16|website=patents.justia.com}}</ref> In 1990, Greene was issued a patent entitled "Latex based adhesive prepared by emulsion polymerization" for the invention of a latex based pressure sensitive adhesive for coating conventional substrates to form an adhesive tape.<ref>{{Cite web|title=US Patent for Latex based adhesive prepared by emulsion polymerization Patent (Patent # 4,968,740 issued November 6, 1990) - Justia Patents Search|url=https://patents.justia.com/patent/4968740|access-date=2020-08-16|website=patents.justia.com}}</ref>

After decades of contribution to the science of polymers, she died in Midland on June 16, 1995.<ref name="Blacksciencefictionsociety-2020" />

==Philanthropy==
[[File:Bettye Washington Greene 1970.tif|200px|thumb|Greene in 1970]]
Greene was a [[charter member]] of the Midland, Michigan Alumni Chapter of the [[Delta Sigma Theta]] [[sorority]], a national public service group emphasizing work with African American women.<ref name=Othmeralia>{{cite web|last=Kativa|first=Hillary|title=From African-American History to Women's History Month: Today we celebrate Dr. Bettye Greene|date=March 2014 |url=http://othmeralia.tumblr.com/post/78212258500/from-african-american-history-to-womens-history|publisher=Chemical Heritage Foundation|access-date=22 March 2014}}</ref> The Midland chapter was chartered in 1984.<ref name=Midland>{{cite web|title=Our History|url=http://www.midlandmidst.org/our-history.html|publisher=Midland Alumnae Chapter|access-date=1 April 2014}}</ref><ref name=Sorority>{{cite news|last=Wade|first=Cheryl|title=Delta Sigma Theta Sorority (Midland chapter) brings women together to celebrate 30th|url=http://www.ourmidland.com/news/delta-sigma-theta-sorority-midland-chapter-brings-women-together-to/article_72b3b46b-96b0-5d7e-b236-8ae3822a3691.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140401143919/http://www.ourmidland.com/news/delta-sigma-theta-sorority-midland-chapter-brings-women-together-to/article_72b3b46b-96b0-5d7e-b236-8ae3822a3691.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 1, 2014|access-date=1 April 2014|newspaper=Midland Daily News|date=15 March 2014}}</ref>

== Acknowledgements ==
28 years following her death, the [[National Historic Chemical Landmarks|National Historical Chemical Landmark]] (NHCL) was awarded to Greene by [[American Chemical Society|The American Chemical Society]] (ACS). The celebration, which took place on October 27, 2023, was held at Wayne State University in Detroit, Michigan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bettye Washington Greene, Ph.D. |url=https://www.acs.org/education/whatischemistry/landmarks/greene.html |access-date=2025-03-01 |website=American Chemical Society |language=en}}</ref>

== Patents ==
Greene held a number of US patents including a latex-based adhesive using a carboxylic acid copolymerizing agent, and latex polymers with phosphates used as coatings:<ref name=Patents>{{cite web|title=Patents by Inventor Bettye W. Greene|url=http://patents.justia.com/inventor/bettye-w-greene|publisher=Justia Patents|access-date=22 March 2014}}</ref><ref name="9 black chemists you should know about" />

* 4968740: Latex-based [[adhesive]] prepared by [[emulsion polymerization]]
* 4609434: Composite sheet prepared with stable latexes containing [[phosphorus]] surface groups
* 4506057: Stable latexes containing phosphorus surface groups
